The Nonfiction Hotlist curates and champions exceptional nonfiction storytelling, connecting creators with audiences, industry opportunities, and sustainable pathways forward.

Through thoughtful conversation, community building and curiosity we’re discovering new and unexpected ways to offer support to creators at any stage of their journey, while also joining forces with long-standing industry organizations who seek meaningful change.
## about
### Hear From Our Storytellers
## values

- We lead with generosity, respect, and thoughtful relationship-building.

- We convene rather than gatekeep, creating spaces where storytellers, funders, and audiences engage directly with projects and each other.

- We believe collaboration within a community creates alchemy impossible to replicate, and building with a village leads to the best work.

- Everyone is invited.

# **The 2026**

# **Hotlist is**

# **Open!**

Submissions are open!

The 2026 Hotlist is a curated slate of standout nonfiction works in progress, spanning documentary features, shorts, series, podcasts, and reality.

We connect creators with audiences, industry opportunities, and partners who can move a project forward.

Deadline to Submit **September 25th, 2026**

items.title: Yahoo Inc
items.excerpt:
Yahoo Media Group and The Nonfiction Hotlist are teaming up to create a new pathway for nonfiction filmmakers to showcase their work to a global audience. Through the partnership, Yahoo will continue to grow its video offering by promoting and distributing 20 short documentary films curated from open call submissions. The Nonfiction Hotlist, a leading documentary content curation and distribution platform known for identifying exceptional stories and connecting filmmakers with major distribution opportunities, will oversee the entire curatorial process.
By combining the distribution of Yahoo with the deep industry expertise and curatorial rigor of The Nonfiction Hotlist, the partnership aims to bring meaningful visibility, awareness, and monetization to great filmmakers and their films.
Yahoo will distribute the selected films across its properties, including yahoosports.tv and its Yahoo Sports Network and Yahoo Finance FAST channels.
Yahoo will further amplify the films with additional content such as filmmaker interviews, behind-the-scenes features, and in-depth companion articles.
Selected filmmakers will also be paid for their work, ensuring fair compensation for creators.

Yahoo Media Group and [The Nonfiction Hotlist](https://nonfictionhotlist.com/) are teaming up to create a new pathway for nonfiction filmmakers to showcase their work to a global audience. Through the partnership, Yahoo will continue to grow its video offering by promoting and distributing 20 short documentary films curated from open call submissions. The Nonfiction Hotlist, a leading documentary content curation and distribution platform known for identifying exceptional stories and connecting filmmakers with major distribution opportunities, will oversee the entire curatorial process.

By combining the distribution of Yahoo with the deep industry expertise and curatorial rigor of The Nonfiction Hotlist, the partnership aims to bring meaningful visibility, awareness, and monetization to great filmmakers and their films.

- Yahoo will distribute the selected films across its properties, including [yahoosports.tv](http://yahoosports.tv/) and its *Yahoo Sports Network* and *Yahoo Finance* FAST channels.

- Yahoo will further amplify the films with additional content such as filmmaker interviews, behind-the-scenes features, and in-depth companion articles.

- Selected filmmakers will also be paid for their work, ensuring fair compensation for creators.

Beginning today, filmmakers can submit their projects for consideration in the following six categories: 1) Sports and Athleticism; 2) Business and Economics; 3) Science, Innovation and Technology; 4) Nature and Environment; 5) Arts and Culture; 6) Biography and Lifestyle. Films will be selected based on artistic merit, powerful storytelling, and cultural relevance.
#### Read the whole article [here](https://www.yahooinc.com/press/yahoo-media-group-and-the-nonfiction-hotlist-partner-to-expand-reach-and-recognition-for-documentary-short-films)

[Yahoo](https://deadline.com/tag/yahoo/) Media Group and [The Nonfiction Hotlist](https://deadline.com/tag/the-nonfiction-hotlist/) have announced a partnership that will see Yahoo promote and distribute 20 short docs across a variety of genres to a global audience.

The Nonfiction Hotlist – “a leading documentary content curation and distribution platform known for identifying exceptional stories and connecting filmmakers with major distribution opportunities” — will oversee the curatorial process. Beginning today and running through March 6, filmmakers can submit their projects for consideration (find the submission portal [here](https://nonfictionhotlist.com/yahooxnfh))…

Yahoo Media Group and The Nonfiction Hotlist are teaming up to create a new pathway for nonfiction filmmakers to showcase their work to a global audience. Through this partnership, Yahoo will promote and distribute **20 short documentary films** curated from open call submissions.

The Nonfiction Hotlist, a leading documentary content curation and distribution platform known for identifying exceptional stories and connecting filmmakers with major distribution opportunities, will oversee the entire curatorial process.
## Opportunity

- **Global Distribution** - Films will be distributed across Yahoo properties, including yahoosports.tv, Yahoo Sports Network, and Yahoo Finance FAST channels

- **Compensation** - Selected filmmakers will be paid for their work, ensuring fair compensation for creators

- **Promotional Support** - Yahoo will further amplify the films with additional content including filmmaker interviews, behind-the-scenes features, and in-depth companion articles

- **End date of submission March 6, 2026**
### **Categories:**

#### 1. Sports and Athleticism

#### 2. Business and Economics

#### 3. Science, Innovation and Technology

#### 4. Nature and Environment

#### 5. Arts and Culture

#### 6. Biography and Lifestyle
Films will be selected based on **artistic merit, powerful storytelling,**and**cultural relevance.**
## **Eligibility**
To be eligible for consideration, submitted films must meet the following requirements:

items.q: Format
items.a: Completed short documentaries

items.q: Runtime
items.a: 8 to 40 minutes in length

items.q: Completion Date
items.a: Films must have been finished between January 2023 and March 2026

items.q: Language
items.a: English Spoken or English Subtitled.

items.q: Submission Period
items.a: January 13, 2026 to March 6th, 2026

Yahoo Media Group and The Nonfiction Hotlist are teaming up to create a new pathway for nonfiction filmmakers to showcase their work to a global audience. Through this partnership, Yahoo will promote and distribute **20 short documentary films** curated from open call submissions.

The Nonfiction Hotlist, a leading documentary content curation and distribution platform known for identifying exceptional stories and connecting filmmakers with major distribution opportunities, will oversee the entire curatorial process.
## Opportunity

- **Global Distribution** - Films will be distributed across Yahoo properties, including yahoosports.tv, Yahoo Sports Network, and Yahoo Finance FAST channels

- **Compensation** - Selected filmmakers will be paid for their work, ensuring fair compensation for creators

- **Promotional Support** - Yahoo will further amplify the films with additional content including filmmaker interviews, behind-the-scenes features, and in-depth companion articles

- **End date of submission March 6, 2026**
### **Categories:**

#### 1. Sports and Athleticism

#### 2. Business and Economics

#### 3. Science, Innovation and Technology

#### 4. Nature and Environment

#### 5. Arts and Culture

#### 6. Biography and Lifestyle
Films will be selected based on **artistic merit, powerful storytelling,**and**cultural relevance.**
## **Eligibility**
To be eligible for consideration, submitted films must meet the following requirements:

items.q: Format
items.a: Completed short documentaries

items.q: Runtime
items.a: 8 to 40 minutes in length

items.q: Completion Date
items.a: Films must have been finished between January 2023 and March 2026

items.q: Language
items.a: English Spoken or English Subtitled.

items.q: Submission Period
items.a: January 13, 2026 to March 6th, 2026

### Frequently Asked Questions
Still have questions? Take a look at the FAQ or reach out anytime. If you’re feeling ready, go ahead and apply.

items.q: Is this the Nonfiction Hotlist Version 2?
items.a: No, this is a separate initiative created specifically in partnership with Yahoo for completed short documentaries. The Nonfiction Hotlist Version 2 will launch later in 2026 with a different focus and structure—stay tuned for details.

items.q: Is there a submission fee?
items.a: No, submission is completely free.

items.q: My film was completed prior to 2023. Can I still submit it?
items.a: Unfortunately no. Films must have been completed between January 1, 2023 and March 2026 to be eligible.

items.q: My film is under 8 minutes long or over 40 minutes long. Can I still submit it?
items.a: We're only able to consider films between 8-40 minutes in length for this partnership. If your film falls outside this range, we encourage you to watch for future Nonfiction Hotlist initiatives that may be a better fit.

items.q: What if my film is not complete?
items.a: Please wait to submit until your film is fully finished. We're only reviewing completed films for this partnership.

items.q: Do I need to have the distribution rights to my film?
items.a: Yes. You must either own the distribution rights outright or have authority from the rights holder to license the film to Yahoo.

items.q: Do I need to have all of the footage, music, appearances and other rights cleared?
items.a: Yes. All third-party materials (archival footage, music, appearances, etc.) must be fully cleared (or feasibly clearable) with proper licenses and releases in place. Films with uncleared rights cannot be selected.

items.q: Can I submit it if it has been previously distributed?
items.a: Yes, as long as the rights are currently available.

items.q: Can I submit more than one film?
items.a: Yes, but please limit submissions to three films maximum.

items.q: Who will be reviewing my submission?
items.a: The Nonfiction Hotlist team, along with carefully selected nonfiction industry professionals, will oversee the entire curatorial process - from initial review through final selection.

items.q: When will selected filmmakers be notified?
items.a: Selected filmmakers will be notified in the Spring of 2026.

items.q: What happens if I’m not selected?
items.a: All filmmakers will be notified of their status via email. While we can only select 20 films for this partnership, we encourage you to stay connected with The Nonfiction Hotlist for future opportunities that may be a better fit for your work.

items.q: What rights will Yahoo acquire if my film is selected?
items.a: Selected filmmakers will grant Yahoo a non-exclusive license to distribute the film across Yahoo's platforms and channels for a specified period. You will retain ownership of your film. Specific terms will be detailed in the licensing agreement provided to selected filmmakers.

items.q: Can my film be on other platforms while it's on Yahoo?
items.a: This will be addressed in the licensing agreement for selected films. Questions about exclusivity windows can be discussed if your film is selected.

items.q: What will selected filmmakers receive?
items.a: Selected filmmakers will receive licensing fees for their work, ensuring fair compensation. Films will be distributed across Yahoo's properties including [yahoosports.tv](http://yahoosports.tv), Yahoo Sports Network, and Yahoo Finance FAST channels, with promotional support including filmmaker interviews, behind-the-scenes features, and companion articles.

items.q: What is the Nonfiction Hotlist?
items.a: A curated list of standout nonfiction projects, spanning documentary features, shorts, series, podcasts, and reality, connecting creators with audiences, industry opportunities, and partners who can move projects forward.

items.q: What does it cost to submit?
items.a: Nothing. Submission is free, and it stays free through every stage of the process.

items.q: What is the deadline to submit?
items.a: September 9th, 2026

items.q: Can I submit multiple projects?
items.a: Yes. Submit as many as you'd like, just be intentional about what you put forward.

items.q: Can I submit a project I've already pitched?
items.a: Yes. Widely pitched, never pitched, fully financed, or still looking for support, if it's a project you believe in, it's eligible.

items.q: I submitted to the first Nonfiction Hotlist. Can I submit again?
items.a: Yes. Projects evolve, and yours may be in a different stage than it was last time. Each cycle is reviewed by a new pool of reviewers alongside a different slate of projects, so every submission gets a fresh look.

items.q: What materials should I submit?
items.a: Title, logline, and any supporting materials you're comfortable sharing: pitch decks, sizzle reels, trailers, or anything else that helps us understand the project.

items.q: Does my project need to be finished before I submit?
items.a: No. The 2026 Hotlist is built for works in progress. Anything from a rough cut on down is welcome: treatment, early footage, assembly, wherever you are. This isn't about who has the most polished cut; it's about the strength of the story and the commitment and care of the team behind it.

items.q: Who sees my submission, and is it confidential?
items.a: Only our reviewers and internal team have access to your materials, and everything stays strictly confidential. Nothing is shared publicly or outside our review process without your approval.

items.q: Who reviews the submissions?
items.a: A paid reviewer cohort pulled from across the nonfiction industry: producers, directors, editors, executives, journalists, and programmers from different corners of the field.

items.q: How are projects selected?
items.a: Every submission is reviewed by multiple people and scored against a shared rubric: excellence in storytelling, originality, emotional impact, crowd appeal, and cultural relevance. Reviewers also meet to discuss and debate projects beyond the scores, and every selection is checked for legal and eligibility clearance before it's confirmed.

items.q: What if a reviewer knows me or my project personally?
items.a: They recuse themselves from scoring it. Every reviewer agrees to a conflict-of-interest and confidentiality policy before each cycle begins.

items.q: How big is the list, and how does it break down by format?
items.a: The 2026 Hotlist is one list of 20-25 projects, mixing formats within: documentary feature, documentary short, podcast, series, and reality. There's no fixed number of slots per format. We're building the strongest possible slate, wherever it comes from.

items.q: Can I submit a project that crosses formats?
items.a: Yes. Series/podcast hybrids, docu-reality crossovers, whatever the project actually is. Submit under whichever format fits best and note the crossover in your materials.

items.q: What happens to strong projects that don't make the final 20-25?
items.a: Not making the list isn't the same as not being valuable. We're building more ways to connect projects that don't make the final cut with opportunities and community, and that work is expanding in 2026.

items.q: How many projects were submitted / selected last cycle?
items.a: Our first cycle drew 639 submissions. We selected 23 for the list.

items.q: What happens if my project is selected?
items.a: We'll reach out directly with next steps and a timeline for the list going public.

items.q: Is there any pay or compensation if my project is selected?
items.a: No. The Hotlist isn't a grant or funding program. We never ask for money and never take any stake in your project, you keep 100% of your IP.

items.q: What does inclusion on the Hotlist lead to?
items.a: Real industry exposure: your project on a published, curated list that reaches filmmakers, producers, executives, and investors. Beyond publication, we stay a resource as your project moves forward, and selected filmmakers join a monthly gathering to connect with fellow creators.

items.q: What's the time commitment if my project is selected?
items.a: Almost none. Beyond reviewing and approving your listing, there's no required commitment. We're happy to be a resource for strategy, feedback, and guidance as your project moves forward.

items.q: When do submissions open?
items.a: Now open.

items.q: When will the Nonfiction Hotlist be released?
items.a: November.

items.q: Where will the list be released?
items.a: The Nonfiction Hotlist is distributed as a published list to our industry newsletter and made available to the wider media community. It will live in our instagram link in bio. If you haven’t seen the [2025 Nonfiction Hotlist](/the-2025-hotlist)please check it out before submitting. [Join the mailing list here to receive it.](https://nonfictionhotlist.com/home#contact)

items.q: How can I support the Nonfiction Hotlist?
items.a: If you're interested in supporting the Nonfiction Hotlist, we'd love to hear from you. [Contact Us Here](mailto:info@nonfictionhotlist.com?)

blocks.text: ## Submissions

Submit your documentary feature, short, series, podcast, or reality project, still in progress. Every submission gets genuine consideration from nonfiction professionals, reviewed for craft, originality, impact and potential.
## Before You Begin

#### We are requesting links, documents, and info about your project. Please have the following items ready:

- Private password-free links to audio/visual materials (sizzle reels, work samples, etc)

- Written materials and pitch decks **(max 25mb)**

- Links to your social media (instagram, linkedin, etc)

- Links to personal or business and other biographical websites

- Bios for you and your creative team
